title: Hotel design: how to plan the guest rooms, lobby and restaurant
seo_title: Hotel design: guest rooms, lobby and restaurant
description: Hotel design: the standard room, a mock-up room before roll-out, hard-wearing materials, lobby and restaurant. What to decide before style. Design from $30/m².
lead: In a hotel, design is counted in money: how many minutes it takes to clean a room, how many years the corridor flooring will last, whether someone from the street will walk into the restaurant. Here is how hotel design works, from the standard room to the lobby and restaurant, and what should be decided before a style is chosen.

body: h2
Where hotel design begins
p

The first question is who the guest is and how long they stay. A business traveller for one night, a family for a week and a couple for a weekend expect different things from a room: a desk, a kitchenette or a bathtub with a view. The answer determines the room types, the area of the public spaces and the budget per room. Style is chosen after that.
p
The brief for the designer should state:
ul
the format: city hotel, boutique hotel, aparthotel, country resort
the number of rooms and their types
who will operate the hotel and what they require of back-of-house areas
whether there will be a restaurant, bar, spa or conference hall
the budget and the opening date
h2
The standard room: one scheme for the whole room stock
p

A room is designed as a product that is then repeated dozens of times. Furniture, lighting, sanitaryware and textiles are identical in all rooms of one type: this makes them easier to buy in a batch, repair and replace. The layout is standard too: an entrance area with a wardrobe and a place for a suitcase, a bathroom next to the service shaft, a bedroom with a workspace by the window.
p
A guest judges a room by details that are often missed in a residential interior:
ul
sockets on both sides of the bed and at the desk
a master light switch at the entrance and by the bed
curtains that black out the room completely
doors and walls that keep out corridor noise
a shelf in the shower, hooks and a place for wet towels
a luggage rack, so the suitcase does not end up on the bed
h2
A mock-up room before roll-out
p

Before ordering furniture for the entire hotel, it is worth completing one room in full: finishes, furniture, lighting and textiles. It is used to test what a rendering does not show. Is it easy for a housekeeper to change the linen and clean under the bed, do the wardrobe doors hit the entrance door, how does the lighting look in the evening, are there enough hooks.
p

Corrections are made to the drawings and the specification, and only then are the remaining rooms started. A mistake in one room costs little; repeated in every room, it is multiplied across the whole room stock.
h2
Materials that stand up to a hotel
p
A hotel room wears out faster than an apartment: suitcases, housekeeping trolleys, frequent cleaning. So materials are chosen by how they age and how they clean.
ul
floors: hard-wearing coverings in rooms and corridors, with no thresholds in the trolley’s path
walls: washable paint, corner protection and protection around the luggage rack
furniture: durable edges and hardware, upholstery that can be cleaned or replaced
bathroom: large-format tiles with a minimum of joints, wall-hung sanitaryware, a floor drain
textiles: fabrics that withstand frequent washing
p

Furniture, lighting and textiles for standard rooms are best ordered in a batch directly from factories in China, including made-to-order pieces by size, colour and material. Delivery takes 35–70 days, so the specification is agreed early. A list of items is given in the article on [hotel furniture procurement](/en/blog/hotel-furniture-procurement-turnkey).
h2
Lobby and reception
p

The lobby creates the first impression and is at the same time a workplace for staff. The reception desk is positioned so that the receptionist can see the entrance and the lifts, and the guest understands at once where to go. Nearby you need luggage storage, a waiting area and a back office behind the desk.
p

Guest and staff routes are kept apart: linen, waste and food deliveries should not pass through the lobby. In a small hotel the lobby is often combined with a bar or café, and then the space works all day, not only at check-in time.

h2
Restaurant and breakfasts
p

A hotel restaurant has two audiences: guests at breakfast and visitors from the city in the evening. The latter need a separate street entrance or an obvious route through the lobby; otherwise the dining room will stand empty after breakfast.
p

The restaurant’s kitchen, ventilation and drainage are designed together with the hotel: fitting an extract system and a grease trap into a finished building is far harder. That is the subject of the article on [restaurant building services](/en/blog/restaurant-building-services-ventilation-drainage-electrics). An example of a venue where we did both the design and the fit-out is the [Monpark](/en/proekty/monpark) restaurant in central Kyiv.

h2
How much hotel design costs and how we work
p

A hotel design project at CAS costs from $30/m², with a minimum project fee of $2,500. Renovation, construction and procurement are priced from the design: the sum depends on the building services, the number of bathrooms and the equipment. We work across Ukraine and in Europe; in Europe design costs from $45/m², minimum $4,000. For companies registered in Ukraine we invoice with or without VAT, on individual terms; for foreign clients we issue an invoice in dollars or euros and a contract in English.
p

We run a hotel as one team: concept, room-stock planning, design, estimate, works and procurement. You have one manager and photo reports every 1–2 weeks, and the works carry a 12-month warranty. Our projects include Yablu Rest, a space for leisure and conferences, and the concept for the Kitana Beach beach complex in Bodrum. If the hotel is being built from scratch, start with the article on [turnkey mini-hotel construction](/en/blog/turnkey-mini-hotel-construction).
faq: How much does hotel design cost?
A design project costs from $30/m², with a minimum project fee of $2,500. Renovation and procurement are priced from the design after the brief and the site survey.

It is one room completed in full before furniture and materials are ordered for the whole hotel. It is used to check ease of cleaning, lighting, furniture and details, and to correct the specification.
Where should hotel design start: with the rooms or the lobby?
With the format and the room stock: who the guest is, how many rooms and of what types. The lobby, restaurant and style are designed after that.
Do you work with hotels outside Kyiv?
Yes, across Ukraine and in Europe. Prices in Europe are higher: design from $45/m², minimum $4,000.
